📖 How to use

  1. Choose metric or imperial units.
  2. Enter your weight and height.
  3. Read your BSA by the DuBois formula.
  4. Compare with the Mosteller estimate shown for reference.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What is the DuBois formula?

BSA = 0.007184 x weight^0.425 x height^0.725, with weight in kg and height in cm. Published in 1916, still widely used in medicine.

What is BSA used for?

Chemotherapy dosing, burn size assessment, cardiac index, and renal function estimates, among others.

Why show Mosteller too?

Mosteller (square root of weight x height / 3600) is simpler and very close to DuBois; clinicians often cross-check with it.
